clue.text: Huntsmen lost while wandering round Eastern volcano

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the E, enclosing it
letters that wander stray from their places, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunting party has lost its way while roaming around an eastern volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: The huntsmen and the eastern direction look like scenery, but every letter of the answer comes from them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount St Helens is a volcano in Washington State, famous for its 1980 eruption; it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Your items getting rearranged by poltergeists ultimately? Very curious

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are put in a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone finds their belongings moved about by ghosts and is understandably baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting rearranged' turns YOUR ITEMS into MYSTERIOU, and 'ultimately' adds the last letter of poltergeists.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious is strange and puzzling, which is what 'very curious' means in its odd, peculiar sense.

clue.text: Ruled by France excessively, after uprising at ground level

parts.note: to be ruled by someone is to be under them
F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that has risen is read from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: too, as in 'too much', means excessively

explanation.surface: A people long ruled heavily by France finally rise up in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' suggests revolt, but in a down clue it turns the word upwards, so TOO reads OOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Underfoot describes what lies beneath your feet, on the floor or ground surface, the same as the clue phrase.

clue.text: Try raising two different types of mammal

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads upwards, a reversal

parts.note: two mammals: an elk and a cat

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to rear a pair of unlike animals together.
explanation.walkthrough: ELK and CAT, read upwards per 'raising', make the answer; the clue reads as animal husbandry.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a job is to attempt or have a go at it, so it is a synonym of try as a verb.

clue.text: Got upset about facilities on a new downhill ride

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about, around, the slang for toilet
in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the word got reads backwards

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for toilets; bog is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone grew annoyed about the amenities on a new ski run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes TOG; 'facilities' is a polite word for toilets, here the British slang term.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sled ridden down snowy slopes, so it is literally a vehicle for a downhill ride.

clue.text: Surrey town records acknowledgement of merit

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour recognising distinction

explanation.surface: A town in Surrey keeps a register of commendations.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a town in the county of Surrey, famous for its racecourse and the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Be upstanding? Wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing upright means the word is written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to be is to exist, or live

explanation.surface: A command to stand up is answered with a protest that it is the wrong thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be upstanding' is a toast-time command, but here LIVE stands up and reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means morally bad or wicked, a strong synonym of wrong in its ethical sense.

clue.text: Aria, say, very much for bass? Not quite

parts.note: so, as in 'so tired', means very much

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a bass voice is pitched low, so low describes it

explanation.surface: A singer wonders whether an aria suits a bass voice, but it doesn't quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims LOW to LO; 'bass' is the deep voice, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a piece sung by a single voice, so it is an example of a solo performance.

clue.text: Job cut not entirely doing for researcher

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: to dock is to cut, as with wages or a tail

explanation.surface: A post is being eliminated, not completely, which affects an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims DOCK to DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is someone doing research after completing a doctorate, so is a type of academic researcher.

clue.text: Former source of mutton I perceived as form of beef

parts.note: past means former, as in past times
mutton is sheep meat, and a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A diner sees what was once mutton served up as beef instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, spiced and smoked brisket, so it is a prepared kind of beef.

clue.text: Brutal defeat — front of face scratched

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them

indicators.note: this picks out the opening letter of the word for face
scratched means struck out, so that opening letter is removed

parts.note: dial is informal slang for a face

explanation.surface: A savage beating, with the front of someone's face clawed.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAL is slang for face; 'front of ... scratched' deletes its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestial means beastlike in cruelty or savagery, a close synonym of brutal.

clue.text: Weapon brand seeing investment by Prince

indicators.note: investment means being clothed or surrounded, so the word for brand surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to brand with a hot iron is to sear

explanation.surface: A weapons company gets financial backing from a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' reads as finance, but it means enclosing: SEAR goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pointed throwing or thrusting weapon, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Pea-plant and tree in shelter

indicators.note: the tree is placed in the word for shelter

parts.note: lee is shelter from wind, as on the lee side
gum is a tree, the eucalyptus

explanation.surface: A pea plant and a tree are growing under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are plants of the pea family, bearing pods, so a pea plant is a typical one.

clue.text: Resolute, 20, going through fortune to make significant journey

indicators.note: these pieces go through the word for fortune, ending up inside it

parts.note: a pile is a fortune, as in making one's pile
grim means resolute, as in grim determination
20 refers to the answer at 20-down, a metal whose chemical symbol is Ag

explanation.surface: A determined person spends a fortune in metal on a big trip.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to 20-down, the metal whose symbol AG joins GRIM inside PILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey of special meaning, often to a shrine, so a significant journey describes it well.

clue.text: Art lover worried about moving these

indicators.note: the word for worried goes about the shuffled letters

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

indicators.note: moving these letters about puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A collector of art frets about relocating some pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' makes ESTHE; 'worried' as ATE comes from the idiom 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a refined appreciation of beauty and art, so an art lover fits.

clue.text: More than one large animal represented in horse? Not entirely

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged
the word horse is not used in full, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a big animal is portrayed in a horse, and is told not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims HORSE to HORS; 'represented' rearranges that with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoceroses are huge horned mammals; the plural form matches the definition's 'more than one'.

clue.text: Make reference to having quantity of current flowing through holiday spot

indicators.note: the electrical units flow through the word for refer, landing inside it

parts.note: to cite something is to make reference to it
amps measure electric current

explanation.surface: Someone mentions that the holiday spot has electricity running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' sounds like a river or sea flow, but here it is electric current, measured in amps.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is a place for tents and caravans, a common destination for holidays.

clue.text: Energy in old salesperson after elevating sausage

parts.note: pep means energy or vigour

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating lifts the words so they read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A lively elderly salesperson gets a boost after promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevating' reads upwards, giving PERONI; 'in' supplies its own two letters rather than signalling insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried Italian-American salami, so it is a kind of sausage.

clue.text: Determination shown by Marine aboard excellent vessel

indicators.note: the Marine is put aboard, inside, the letters for the fine ship

parts.note: fine means excellent
RM stands for Royal Marine
SS means steamship

explanation.surface: A Marine on a splendid ship shows great resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' places RM inside FINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness is resolve or steadfastness, a synonym of determination.

clue.text: Horse active in elevated region

parts.note: a mount is a horse that is ridden

explanation.surface: A horse is busy in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain is a high landmass rising above its surroundings, so it is an elevated region.

clue.text: Brewery tap, with drunk embracing someone guzzling

indicators.note: the word for drunk embraces, holds within it, the greedy eater

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a pig is a greedy guzzler

explanation.surface: At the brewery tap, a drunk hugs someone knocking back drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'someone guzzling' is a greedy eater, conventionally a pig, not another drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or tap fitted to a cask, the sort used for drawing beer.

clue.text: Metal shard I moved forward

indicators.note: the letter is moved forward, nearer the front of the word for shard

parts.note: a sliver is a shard or splinter

explanation.surface: Someone shifted a metal fragment ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved forward' shifts the I in SLIVER one place towards the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, chemical symbol Ag.

clue.text: Seafood racket attracting detective

parts.note: a racket is a fraud or scam
PI stands for private investigator

explanation.surface: A seafood fraud catches a detective's interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a popular seafood dish.

clue.text: Sorceress left out of magic group?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is taken out of the word

parts.note: the Magic Circle is a British society of magicians

explanation.surface: A witch has been expelled from a society of conjurors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is Britain's best-known club of stage magicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's crew into pigs.

clue.text: European story, probed by Times, backing person living elsewhere

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole is reversed
the multiplication sign probes into, goes inside, the other letters

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A European tale, investigated by a newspaper, supports someone abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probed by' puts X inside ELIE to give ELIXE; 'backing' reverses it. 'Times' looks like the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone banished or living away from their homeland.

clue.text: Dig succeeded, turning up bit of debris

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: turning means the little word up is read the other way round
a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An excavation worked, unearthing a fragment of rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses UP to PU; 'bit of' takes D from debris.
explanation.definitionFit: To spud is to dig with a spud, a narrow spade for weeding, a rare verb sense.

clue.text: Obtain article in spirit

indicators.note: the article goes in the word for spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone acquires an item inside a liquor bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain is to acquire or get, a synonym of obtain.

clue.text: Is inquisitive mostly about attitude in central American region?

indicators.note: the cut word goes about, around, the word for attitude
mostly means most of the word, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: someone who pries is being inquisitive
an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: Someone nosey wonders about the mood in a part of the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the S, leaving PRIE. 'central American' means the middle of North America, not Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairies are the grasslands of the central North American interior.

clue.text: Abuse Stradivarius, perhaps, and trombone's case

parts.note: Stradivari made violas as well as violins, so a Strad may be one

indicators.note: a word's case is its outside, so its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Mistreating a valuable Strad and a trombone's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outside letters of trombone, T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate is to treat with disrespect or abuse, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Material for courses beginning to detail less visible military force

indicators.note: beginning to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: inner parts are hidden from view, less visible than outer ones
a service is a branch of the armed forces

explanation.surface: A detachment from a hidden military unit provides training material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests training, but means courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a set of plates and dishes on which the courses of a meal are served.
